sourceFile: Diocese of Montana Prayer Cycle, a Google Calendar (calendar id q57av3va3lcfaps5lmg4nqgj8k@group.calendar.google.com, titled "Diocese of Montana Prayer Cycle") embedded on https://diomontana.com/prayer-cycle-calendar/; fetched directly via its public ICS export at https://calendar.google.com/calendar/ical/q57av3va3lcfaps5lmg4nqgj8k%40group.calendar.google.com/public/basic.ics since the diocesan page itself only embeds a JS-rendered iframe with no static event data.
notes: The diocesan page (https://diomontana.com/prayer-cycle-calendar/) embeds a Google Calendar widget with no static event data in the page's own HTML -- a plain fetch of the page returns only the iframe shell. The page source does expose the iframe's own src=, a calendar.google.com/calendar/embed URL naming the underlying calendar id (q57av3va3lcfaps5lmg4nqgj8k@group.calendar.google.com); that calendar id's public ICS export (calendar.google.com/calendar/ical/.../public/basic.ics) returns the real event data with no authentication or JS rendering required, and was used as the actual source for this transcription.

The roster's own research note for this diocese says coverage is only 'September 2026 onward' (63 events spot-checked in September 2026). The calendar feed actually turned out to hold dated entries for the diocese's ENTIRE 2026 calendar cycle, January 1 through December 27, 2026 (276 distinct dates, 600 total subject entries across them) -- more complete than the roster's own note anticipated. All of it is transcribed here since it is genuine dated 2026 content the diocese has already published in its live calendar, not fabricated. September 2026 alone holds 55 events in this transcription, close to but not exactly the roster's spot-checked count of 63 (the small difference is not explained and not corrected here).

89 calendar days between 2026-01-01 and 2026-12-27 have no event at all in the source calendar (leaving 276 populated dates) -- these are gaps in the diocese's own calendar, not omissions in this transcription. The calendar's own 2026 coverage also stops after December 27; no 2026 entries exist for December 28-31.

This is a daily household-and-parish cycle, not a Sunday-only cycle: most dates name 1-3 individual people, couples, or families with no congregation or place given alongside them at all -- recorded here as `category` subjects (per this corpus's rule that a calendar of bare names with no attached congregation is `category`, not `parish`), since the source itself does not say which parish, if any, each such person belongs to. Interspersed roughly weekly (mostly on Sundays) is a 'parish of the week' entry that DOES explicitly pair one specific congregation with a place (recorded as a `parish` subject, e.g. 'St. Mark's, Anaconda') alongside that congregation's own clergy/wardens/deacons named with their titles (recorded as `category` subjects, e.g. 'Sadie Koppelberger, Rector', since a title-holder's name is not itself a place/congregation). Each of roughly 26 congregations appears in this role on two non-consecutive weeks across the year.

The underlying source is a live calendar feed, not a printed table with a fixed row order -- when multiple subjects land on the same date, they are recorded here in the order the calendar feed itself returns them for that date (there is no separate table layout to check them against).
liturgicalNote is null throughout: the source's own event titles never carry a liturgical Sunday/feast label of any kind (unlike some other dioceses' cycles), so none is recorded.

Numerous spelling/name variants for the same recurring person or place are preserved exactly as printed on each individual date rather than normalized to one spelling, per this corpus's standing rule against silently correcting a source's own document -- for example (not exhaustive): 'Jocelyn & Jermiah Snyder' (2026-01-23) vs. 'Jocelyn & Jeremiah Snider' elsewhere; 'Donnell & Janet O'Flynn' (2026-03-02) vs. 'Donnel & Janet O'Flynn' elsewhere; 'Maurice & Marybeth Champion-Garth' vs. 'Champion-Garthe' on other dates; 'Dorcie & Mark Dvarishkis' vs. 'Dvarshkis' (2026-03-31) vs. 'Dvarshkis' (2026-05-13 area); 'Tim & Linda Ljundggren' (2026-02-25) vs. 'Ljunggren' elsewhere; 'Julianna Olliff' vs. 'Juliana Olliff' vs. 'Olliff'; 'Christine Whiteside' vs. 'Christina Whiteside' (2026-11-06); 'All Saint's, Big Sky' (2026-04-26) vs. 'All Saints, Big Sky' (2026-08-09, no apostrophe) for the very same congregation; 'Church of the Trinity, Jeffers-Ennis' (2026-01-11) vs. 'Church of the Trinity, Jeffers' (2026-12-13, place given without '-Ennis') for the very same congregation; 'Karen King & Judith Kesot' (2026-01-06) vs. 'Karen King' alone (2026-08-11).

'Holy Troy, Trinity' (2026-04-05) is transcribed exactly as printed in the source, split into name 'Holy Troy' and place 'Trinity' per the source's own comma placement, per this corpus's rule against silently correcting a source. Checked directly against the same underlying calendar feed's entries for this same recurring slot in every other year from 2013 through 2025, all of which instead read 'Holy Trinity, Troy' -- this 2026 instance looks like an accidental transposition in the diocese's own calendar, disclosed here (and per-subject) rather than corrected.

'Togendowagan Society, St. Peter's Cathedral' (2026-01-04) and 'Togendowagen Society at St. Peter's Cathedral' (2026-12-06) both name the same group at the cathedral in Helena, using two different spellings of 'Togendowagan'/'Togendowagen' and two different phrasings ('X, Y' vs. 'X at Y') on their respective dates, each preserved exactly as printed. Both are recorded as `category` subjects rather than `parish`, since neither gives a town/place separate from the cathedral's own name the way every other parish entry does; the cathedral itself is recorded separately as a `parish` subject (name 'St. Peter's Cathedral', place 'Helena') only where the source's own 2026-11-29 entry gives it that way.
